text:
maria: Heads up — merged a TF module change that added `az_affinity` to the gpupool module. CI passed but gitops detected drift against prod gpufleet. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/789
jon: saw the plan. It wants to start replacing nodes because `az_affinity` goes from null -> string. Provider schema change maybe.
alex: can you paste the `terraform plan` snippet? :eyes:
maria: snippet below:
```diff
- resource \"redwood_gpu_pool\" \"main\" {
-   az_affinity = null
+ resource \"redwood_gpu_pool\" \"main\" {
+   az_affinity = \"zone-a\"
```
sre-oncall: That replacement will churn nodes across AZs. We should gate the module bump and avoid an automatic roll in prod. Rollback PR?
jon: opened revert pin PR to go back to v2.18.0: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/790. CI added a hold label too.
infra-ci: pipeline flagged: `module version bump requires manual approval` — hold label applied by policy.
maria: Proposed plan: 1) hold the bump in monorepo, 2) reconcile prod gpufleet back to stable module, 3) add a compatibility gate in GitOps that runs TF compatibility checks (AZ affinity + type checks) before auto-merging.
alex: I can prototype a gate: run `terraform plan -var 'az_affinity=null'` in an ephemeral workspace and fail on replacements or type mismatches. Quick prototype:
```bash
PLAN=$(terraform plan -input=false)
if echo "$PLAN" | grep -E "replaced|type mismatch"; then
  echo \"compatibility check failed\"
  exit 1
fi
```
deploy-bot: Created ticket INFRA-1234 to add module compatibility tests + module version guard in GitOps.
maria: Also saw a KMS schema warning in the plan: `type mismatch: string vs object for kms_key`. We need a schema-preserving shim or optional input handling — this could break imports.
jon: yep, kms field change is risky. We should accept both shapes or add a migration step.
alex: plan to add a small compat shim: `kms_key = try(var.kms_key, var.kms_key.id)` and document the change in the module upgrade notes.
sre-oncall: urgent: block any gpupool applies in prod until compatibility gate lands. If we apply drift we risk node rotation and possible capacity gaps — SLA risk.
maria: TL;DR: revert module bump + hold merge, add CI gate that runs `terraform plan` diffs & type checks, implement shim for kms, run canary in staging, then roll forward via canary pipeline. Agree?
jon: yup — merging revert + hold label now. :thumbsup:
alex: I'll open the gate hook PR today and wire it into the gitops pipeline.
infra-ci: ephemeral workspace `staging-compat-check` created for runs.
deploy-bot: INFRA-1234 assigned to @alex, @jon. ETA EOD.
